findings.evidence: The refusal a target-less run's landing raises prescribes `workspace.py establish {run} {ticket_id}` 'from the checkout driving this run -- it replays against the existing tree and records the target'. At this revision an establishment without --repo has named=False, so _derived reads tickets_store.integration_target(run) instead of recording one; the prescribed command replays at exit 0 and records nothing (probe reading above). The refusal is therefore a dead end: the only recovery is `--repo <checkout>`, which nothing in the refusal names. This is the very failure path the unit created -- the Details named this file's refusal text and said to carry it -- and the ordinary driver flow reaches it: the host block lists `--workspace` as optional on `tickets.py do`, the facade now passes no --repo without it, so a run driven from inside its own repository without --workspace records no target and its first land refuses into this text. The existing pin test_a_run_that_recorded_no_target_is_refused_with_the_establishment asserts only the substring 'workspace.py establish testrun T1' and so cannot see the staleness.
findings.smallest_change: Make the refusal name the flag: `Run 'workspace.py establish {run} {ticket_id} --repo <the checkout this run integrates into>' -- it replays against the existing tree and records the target -- then land again`, and tighten the pin to assert `--repo` in the remedy (its can-fail reading: drop the flag from the sentence).

findings.evidence: The same cause seen from the driver: after this revision `--workspace` is load-bearing for whether a run can ever land, yet `tickets.py do`'s payload says nothing when the establishment records no target (the establish body carries `integration: None` silently) and the host block still spells the flag as optional with no consequence named. A driver learns the rule only from the F1 refusal, one landing later.
findings.smallest_change: Successor scope (the host block is at its 400-word budget and the facade is outside this unit's Goal): when an isolation-required, non-judging establishment leaves the run with no recorded target, the do payload carries one line naming `--workspace` as what fixes it; or the host block's `[--workspace <tree>]` gains the three words that say the first code do names it.

findings.evidence: Both discard file_once's `(outcome, refusal)` return. A note that could not be filed (unreadable ticket, atomic write refused) leaves no trace in the step report; the docstring calls this best-effort so the refusal reaches the caller, which is right for ordering but wrong for silence -- the reader of a later resolution note cannot tell a never-refused landing from one whose conflict note was lost.
findings.smallest_change: Carry the filing outcome into the workspace-integrate step dict (`"note": outcome`, and the refusal text under `note_error` when one comes back), leaving the landing's own verdict untouched.
